claim: Chillon Castle is officially the most visited historical monument in Switzerland, open daily April–September 9:00–19:00 with adult admission CHF 15; S5 regional trains run hourly from Lausanne to Veytaux-Chillon, a 6-minute walk away.
quote: S5 regional trains depart hourly to Veytaux-Chillon station, a 6-minute walk away. ... The site is recognized as 'the most visited historical monument in Switzerland.'

claim: From Lausanne to Veytaux-Chillon by train takes around 35 minutes with departures every 10–20 minutes; via Montreux it is 20 minutes to Montreux then 4 minutes onward.
quote: The train from Lausanne to Château de Chillon (Veytaux-Chillon) takes 35 minutes, with trains leaving roughly every 10 to 20 minutes.

claim: Montreux's lakeside Place du Marché hosts the bronze Freddie Mercury statue (unveiled 1996, by Czech sculptor Irena Sedlecká) in his Wembley-1986 pose, freely accessible on the flat Riviera promenade.
quote: The bronze statue of Czech sculptor Irena Sedlecká was unveiled in 1996 and stands on the Place du Marché directly on the lakeside promenade.

claim: Vevey is 20 minutes by train from Lausanne and combines Chaplin's World, the Alimentarium food museum, the giant lake-set Fork sculpture, and a walkable lakeside in one compact destination.
quote: Vevey sits on the main rail line between Lausanne (20 minutes) and Montreux (8 minutes), with frequent trains throughout the day.

claim: The Fork in front of the Alimentarium in Vevey is an 8-metre stainless-steel sculpture by Jean-Pierre Zaugg, installed 1995 for the museum's 10th anniversary and entered in the Guinness World Records in 2014 as the world's tallest fork.
quote: The Fork is made of stainless steel, 8 metres high and 1.3 metres wide. ... It has held the record in the Guinness World Records since 2014 as the world's tallest fork.

claim: Chaplin's World occupies the Manoir de Ban above Vevey in Corsier-sur-Vevey, where Charlie Chaplin spent the last 25 years of his life; the museum pairs his family home with a studio area for interactive film exhibits.
quote: Chaplin lived the final 25 years of his life in the large house Manoir de Ban in Corsier-sur-Vevey on the slopes overlooking Lake Geneva and the Alps.

claim: Gruyères day-trip from Lausanne takes about 1h15–1h30 by train with one or two transfers and centres on the 13th-century castle, La Maison du Gruyère cheese factory, HR Giger Museum, and a cobblestoned medieval town.
quote: The journey takes approximately 45 minutes by car or 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes by train with one or two transfers.

claim: There is no direct train from Lausanne to Gruyères; the fastest route runs via Palézieux in about 1h 45m with typical changes at Palézieux/Bulle.
quote: There is no direct train from Lausanne to Gruyères. You can take a train from Lausanne to Gruyères via Palézieux in around 1h 45m.

claim: The HR Giger Museum sits in St-Germain Castle in medieval Gruyères and houses the largest collection of the Alien designer's paintings, sculptures, furniture, and film sets; summer hours run 10:00–18:00 weekdays and to 18:30 weekends.
quote: Summer opening hours (March 29, 2026 – November 1, 2026) Monday to Friday from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday and Sunday from 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.

claim: The CGN N1 ferry from Lausanne-Ouchy to Évian-les-Bains crosses Lake Geneva in about 35 minutes for CHF 22 second class / CHF 31 first, but from 2026 CGN has roughly halved crossings, concentrating them around commuter hours.
quote: From 2026, the number of ferries crossing Lake Geneva is reduced, with passenger ferry boats mostly operating during commuting hours.

claim: CGN publishes the official 2026 timetable and ticketing for Lake Geneva passenger boats including the Lausanne-Ouchy–Évian-les-Bains N1 line.
